result.instructions: Tools for packagecloud, hosted by usefulapi.io. If the user is new or asks what this server can do, suggest requests such as: "Which package repositories do I have, and how many packages are in each?"; "List all versions of the package my-agent in my main repository."; "How many times was my release repository installed this month?". Read-only tools never change data; ask the user before a tool that creates, changes or deletes packagecloud data. Free plan: 50 tool calls per month. Run packagecloud_usage_status to see the calls used this month. If the user asks for something none of these tools can do, tell the user and, with their OK, run packagecloud_request_feature to record the request. Paid plan: Pro (unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month), $9/month or $90/year). Pro can be cancelled at any time and then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. When the user wants more calls or reaches the limit, run packagecloud_upgrade (plan "monthly" or "yearly"); it returns a payment link for the user to open. packagecloud_cancel_subscription cancels Pro at the end of the paid period.

tools.name: packagecloud_list_repositories
tools.title: List repositories
tools.description: List the package repositories of this account: name, fqname (user/repo, used by every other tool), privacy, package count and last push. include_collaborations adds repositories you collaborate on. GET /repos.

include_collaborations.description: Also list repositories that belong to other accounts but that you collaborate on.

page.description: Page number, from 1 (default 1). Pass the previous reply's next_page.

per_page.description: Results per page (default 30; the server caps it at its own Max-Per-Page).

tools.name: packagecloud_get_repository
tools.title: Get repository
tools.description: One repository: name, fqname, url, privacy, package count and last push. GET /repos/{user}/{repo}.

repository.description: The repository as "user/repo" (the fqname returned by packagecloud_list_repositories).

tools.name: packagecloud_create_repository
tools.title: Create repository
tools.description: WRITE: create a new, empty package repository in this account (the plan limits how many private ones). Returns the URL of the new repository. POST /repos.

private.description: Create a private repository (default true) or a public one.

tools.name: packagecloud_list_distributions
tools.title: List distributions
tools.description: The Linux distributions and versions packagecloud supports for deb, dsc and rpm packages, with their index_name (for example ubuntu / jammy) and numeric version ids. GET /distributions.

tools.name: packagecloud_list_packages
tools.title: List all packages
tools.description: List every package file in a repository (not grouped), newest data first as the server orders it. Each item carries ready-made URLs: package_url, versions_url, downloads_*_url, promote_url, destroy_url and download_url; pass those to the other package tools. Paged. GET /repos/{user}/{repo}/packages.json.

repository.description: The repository as "user/repo" (the fqname returned by packagecloud_list_repositories).

page.description: Page number, from 1 (default 1). Pass the previous reply's next_page.

per_page.description: Results per page (default 30; the server caps it at its own Max-Per-Page).

tools.name: packagecloud_search_packages
tools.title: Search packages
tools.description: Search a repository by package file name. An empty q returns every package. filter limits by type (rpms, debs, dscs, gem, python, node); dist (for example ubuntu or el/6) overrides filter; arch applies to Alpine/RPM/Debian only. Items carry the same ready-made URLs as list_packages. Paged. GET /repos/{user}/{repo}/search.json.

repository.description: The repository as "user/repo" (the fqname returned by packagecloud_list_repositories).

q.description: Part of the package file name; empty returns all packages.

filter.description: Package type: rpms, debs, dscs, gem, python or node. Ignored when dist is given.

dist.description: Distribution, for example ubuntu or el/6.

arch.description: Architecture, for example x86_64, arm64 or amd64.

page.description: Page number, from 1 (default 1). Pass the previous reply's next_page.

per_page.description: Results per page (default 30; the server caps it at its own Max-Per-Page).

tools.name: packagecloud_list_package_groups
tools.title: List package names by type
tools.description: List the packages of one type, grouped by name with a versions_count and a versions_url (pass that to packagecloud_list_package_versions). Narrow by distro, then version, then arch (each needs the previous one; '*' matches any). Examples: type rpm; type deb + distro ubuntu + version jammy + arch amd64; type gem. GET /repos/{user}/{repo}/packages/{type}[/{distro}[/{version}[/{arch}]]].json.

repository.description: The repository as "user/repo" (the fqname returned by packagecloud_list_repositories).

type.description: Package type: deb, rpm, gem, python, node, java, helm, alpine ...

distro.description: Distribution name, for example ubuntu or el.

version.description: Distribution version name, for example jammy or 7.

arch.description: Architecture, for example amd64 or x86_64.

page.description: Page number, from 1 (default 1). Pass the previous reply's next_page.

per_page.description: Results per page (default 30; the server caps it at its own Max-Per-Page).

tools.name: packagecloud_get_package
tools.title: Get package
tools.description: Details of one package file (size, checksums, dependencies, licenses, download counts and its other URLs). Pass the package_url of an item from list_packages, search_packages or list_package_versions. GET {package_url}.

package_url.description: The package_url of a package object, exactly as returned by the API (a /api/v1/repos/... path).

tools.name: packagecloud_list_package_versions
tools.title: List package versions
tools.description: All versions of one package name (for deb/rpm: per distro, version and architecture). Pass the versions_url of an item from list_package_groups, or derive it from a package object. Paged. GET {versions_url}.

versions_url.description: The versions_url of a package object, exactly as returned by the API (a /api/v1/repos/... path).

page.description: Page number, from 1 (default 1). Pass the previous reply's next_page.

per_page.description: Results per page (default 30; the server caps it at its own Max-Per-Page).

tools.name: packagecloud_get_package_downloads
tools.title: Get package download stats
tools.description: Download statistics of one package version: a count, a time series, or (repository owners only) the detail of each download. Default range is the last 7 days; pass start_date=19700101Z for all time. Pass the package_url of the package; Java and generic files have no download stats. GET {package_url minus .json}/stats/downloads/{count|detail|series/<interval>}.json.

package_url.description: The package_url of a package object, exactly as returned by the API (a /api/v1/repos/... path).

kind.description: count = total, series = per interval, detail = one record per download (owners only).

start_date.description: An ISO 8601 date, for example 20260101Z or 2026-01-01.

end_date.description: An ISO 8601 date, for example 20260101Z or 2026-01-01.

source.description: Only downloads from the "web" or the "cli".

user_agent.description: Only downloads whose user agent equals this.

page.description: Page number, from 1 (default 1). Pass the previous reply's next_page.

per_page.description: Results per page (default 30; the server caps it at its own Max-Per-Page).

tools.name: packagecloud_get_repository_installs
tools.title: Get repository install stats
tools.description: How often a repository was installed (set up on a machine): a count, a time series, or (owners only) the detail of each install, optionally for one distro or distro+version. Default range is the last 7 days; pass start_date=19700101Z for all time. GET /repos/{user}/{repo}/stats/installs[/{distro}[/{version}]]/{count|detail|series/<interval>}.json.

repository.description: The repository as "user/repo" (the fqname returned by packagecloud_list_repositories).

kind.description: count = total, series = per interval, detail = one record per install (owners only; includes host names and IP addresses).

distro.description: Only installs on this distribution, for example ubuntu.

version.description: Only installs on this distribution version, for example jammy (needs distro).

start_date.description: An ISO 8601 date, for example 20260101Z or 2026-01-01.

end_date.description: An ISO 8601 date, for example 20260101Z or 2026-01-01.

user_agent.description: Only downloads whose user agent equals this.

page.description: Page number, from 1 (default 1). Pass the previous reply's next_page.

per_page.description: Results per page (default 30; the server caps it at its own Max-Per-Page).

tools.name: packagecloud_list_gpg_keys
tools.title: List GPG keys
tools.description: The GPG keys of a repository (repository signing keys and package signing keys): name, fingerprint, type and the public key download URL. GET /repos/{user}/{repo}/gpg_keys.json.

repository.description: The repository as "user/repo" (the fqname returned by packagecloud_list_repositories).

tools.name: packagecloud_get_gpg_key
tools.title: Get GPG key
tools.description: One GPG key of a repository by its key name (as returned by list_gpg_keys, for example user-repo-85D7FBF915DFCBC6.pub.gpg). GET /repos/{user}/{repo}/gpg_keys/{keyname}.json.

repository.description: The repository as "user/repo" (the fqname returned by packagecloud_list_repositories).

tools.name: packagecloud_get_readme
tools.title: Get repository README
tools.description: The Markdown README of a repository. GET /repos/{user}/{repo}/readme.json.

repository.description: The repository as "user/repo" (the fqname returned by packagecloud_list_repositories).

tools.name: packagecloud_create_readme
tools.title: Create repository README
tools.description: WRITE: create the Markdown README of a repository. Use append_readme to add to an existing one. POST /repos/{user}/{repo}/readme.json.

repository.description: The repository as "user/repo" (the fqname returned by packagecloud_list_repositories).

tools.name: packagecloud_append_readme
tools.title: Append to repository README
tools.description: WRITE: append Markdown to the existing README of a repository (existing text is kept). Not idempotent: calling it twice appends twice. PATCH /repos/{user}/{repo}/readme.json.

repository.description: The repository as "user/repo" (the fqname returned by packagecloud_list_repositories).

body.description: Markdown to append to the README.

tools.name: packagecloud_promote_package
tools.title: Promote (move) package
tools.description: WRITE, DESTRUCTIVE: MOVE a package file to another repository (for example staging -> production). It no longer exists in the source repository afterwards, and its download statistics are cleared. Pass the promote_url of the package object and the destination as user/repo. POST {promote_url}.

promote_url.description: The promote_url of a package object, exactly as returned by the API (a /api/v1/repos/... path).

destination.description: The destination repository as "user/repo" (it must already exist).

scope.description: Only for a scoped Node.js package: the scope including the @, for example @example.

tools.name: packagecloud_delete_package
tools.title: Delete (yank) package
tools.description: WRITE, DESTRUCTIVE AND IRREVERSIBLE: delete one package file from its repository (a gem is yanked). Clients that depend on it will break. Pass the destroy_url of the package object and repeat its file name (the last path segment, for example jake-1.0-2.el6.x86_64.rpm) as confirm_filename. DELETE {destroy_url}.

destroy_url.description: The destroy_url of a package object, exactly as returned by the API (a /api/v1/repos/... path).

confirm_filename.description: The package file name, exactly as in the last segment of destroy_url (the 'filename' field of the package).

scope.description: Only for a scoped Node.js package: the scope including the @, for example @example.
